title: Fine-grained descending control of steering in walking Drosophila.
source_locator: Results, 'Different descending neurons drive distinctive leg gestures'; Fig. 4A-C; Fig. S6G (left)
quote: In experimental flies, we found that a pulse of light triggered an ipsilateral turn, with no change in forward velocity as compared with controls
mapping_basis: The paper's name DNa02 is the MANC type name in type_list.csv; hemidrivers R75C10AD/R87D07DBD are those of SS00730, listed as DNa02 in driver_lines.csv.
stimulation: 620/60 nm light, 0.09 mW/mm2 on head and thorax, 200 ms pulses (randomly interleaved with 2 s pulses that had similar transient effects)
type_coverage: one of the two DNa02 cells (unilateral mosaic expression)
sensory_condition: norpA[P24] blind background; walking on air-supported ball; head capsule closed; wings removed
other_cell_types: one type of visual neuron with arbors in the lobula (~2 cells per hemisphere)
a few abdominal ganglion cells in a subset of flies
coordination_notes: Stride length of all three ipsilateral legs shortened, mainly via a shorter return stroke; power stroke largely unaffected; less consistent contralateral effects; step direction of both front and middle legs shifted to pull the body into the turn.
n_flies_note: 8 CsCh+ flies vs 7 no-CsCh controls (genetically identical siblings)
notes: Trials were analysed only if the fly kept a forward velocity >= 1 mm/s from 200 ms before to 200 ms after stimulation (STAR Methods), so this is steering in a fly that was already walking; leg-rhythm fields are not_assessed (PROTOCOL section 3). All six legs were tracked (APT).

title: Fine-grained descending control of steering in walking Drosophila.
source_locator: Results, 'Different descending neurons drive distinctive leg gestures'; Fig. S6A-C
quote: Bilateral activation of DNa02 instead triggered a decrease in forward velocity without a change in the heading direction (Figure S6A).
mapping_basis: The paper's name DNa02 is the MANC type name in type_list.csv; hemidrivers R75C10AD/R87D07DBD are those of SS00730, listed as DNa02 in driver_lines.csv.
stimulation: 620/60 nm light, 0.09 mW/mm2 on head and thorax, 200 ms pulses
type_coverage: both DNa02 cells (mosaic expression in both copies)
sensory_condition: norpA[P24] blind background; walking on air-supported ball; head capsule closed; wings removed
other_cell_types: one type of visual neuron with arbors in the lobula (~2 cells per hemisphere)
a few abdominal ganglion cells in a subset of flies
coordination_notes: Stride length shortened bilaterally, mainly via a shorter return stroke; no significant step-direction change (Fig. S6B-C, S6G).
n_flies_note: 3 bilateral CsCh+ flies vs 7 no-CsCh controls (Fig. S6A)
notes: Separate record because the outcome (slowing, no turn) differs from unilateral stimulation. Same walking-trial inclusion criterion (forward velocity >= 1 mm/s), so the fly was already walking and leg-rhythm fields are not_assessed. behaviour_category 'other' = slowing of ongoing forward walking.

title: Descending networks transform command signals into population motor control.
source_locator: Extended Data Fig. 5e (intact, black traces) and legend; Supplementary Table 5
quote: DNa02 has monosynaptic connections to 18 other DNs and weakly triggers turning. This is quantified as an increase in turning velocity.
mapping_basis: The paper's name DNa02 is the MANC type name in type_list.csv; Supplementary Table 2 gives line SS00730 (75C10-p65ADZp / 87D07-ZpGdbd), listed as DNa02 in driver_lines.csv.
stimulation: 640 nm laser aimed at neck/thorax, 5 s stimulation, 10 trials per fly, 25 s between trials
sensory_condition: on spherical treadmill; wings removed; fly holder filled with saline
n_flies_note: 6 experimental flies x 10 trials; 5 control flies
notes: figure: ED Fig. 5e shows a modest rise in intact turn velocity during the light (intact vs headless P = 0.002, n = 6). Only ball turn and side velocity were reported. Legs were not tracked or described, and the pre-stimulus state for these experiments is not stated, so it is unclear whether stepping started or was already under way. Intact controls also showed a light response (intact vs headless P = 0.047). Line specificity is coded 'clean' because this paper says it chose clean spGAL4 lines; the Cell 2024 and bioRxiv 2020 sources report minor off-target expression for the same line. The paper's connectivity-based 'broadcaster' prediction is not a Pugliese-type simulation score and was not used as evidence.

title: Descending networks transform command signals into population motor control.
source_locator: Extended Data Fig. 5e (headless, blue traces) and legend; Supplementary Table 5; main text 'Network size predicts behavioural necessity'
quote: weakly triggers turning. This is quantified as an increase in turning velocity. This behavior is lost in headless animals.
mapping_basis: The paper's name DNa02 is the MANC type name in type_list.csv; Supplementary Table 2 gives line SS00730, listed as DNa02 in driver_lines.csv.
stimulation: 640 nm laser aimed at neck/thorax, 5 s stimulation, 10 trials per fly, 25 s between trials
sensory_condition: decapitated, neck stump sealed with UV glue, at least 10 min recovery; on spherical treadmill
n_flies_note: 6 headless experimental flies vs 5 headless controls
notes: figure: ED Fig. 5e headless trace is flat. Headless DNa02 vs headless control: turn velocity P = 0.158, side velocity P = 0.085 (Supplementary Table 5). Forward velocity is not reported for DNa02, and no leg movement is described in the text or legend. Headless flies were kept only if their legs moved spontaneously (Methods), so the legs were not motionless, but whether stimulation started or increased stepping cannot be read from turn/side velocity. Legs are therefore coded unclear, not no. effect_on_walking 'none' refers to the measured turn/side velocity only. The headless 'hanging without ground contact' condition appears only in Supplementary Video 4, which was not downloaded, so it has no record.

title: Neural circuit mechanisms for steering control in walking Drosophila
source_locator: Results, 'Contributions of single descending neuron types to steering behavior'; Fig. 8A-C; Methods 'Stochastic ReaChR expression'
quote: In the flies with unilateral expression, we found that light evoked a small average steering bias in the ipsilateral direction
mapping_basis: The paper's name DNa02 is the MANC type name in type_list.csv; Methods name the DNa02 split-Gal4 line SS00730 (DNa02 in driver_lines.csv).
stimulation: 617 nm light from above the head, symmetric, 68 uW/mm2, 0.5 s every 11 s, 150 trials
type_coverage: unilateral expression (one DNa02), scored post hoc by dissection
sensory_condition: walking on spherical treadmill; head cuticle intact, no dissection before behaviour
coordination_notes: Only ball rotational velocity measured; legs not tracked in this experiment.
penetrance: small average ipsilateral bias; unilateral mean outside the 95% CI of a bootstrap null built from bilateral-expression siblings; individual flies varied (Fig. 8C)
n_flies_note: Fig. 8B legend: 16/17 flies (uni/bilateral). Methods: 9 left-only + 8 right-only = 17 unilateral brains, 47 bilateral, 8 none, of 73 experiments
notes: Flies were walking on the ball when light was delivered (Fig. 8A legend), so this is a steering bias in an already-walking fly and leg-rhythm fields are not_assessed. Off-target expression of SS00730 is from the Fig. S8 legend. The 'simulation' in this paper is a statistical bootstrap, not a connectome model.

title: Neural circuit mechanisms for steering control in walking Drosophila
source_locator: Results, 'Contributions of single descending neuron types to steering behavior', paragraph after Fig. 8 legend; Fig. 8B-C (bilateral group)
quote: These effects were likely due to visual startle, because they were indistinguishable in flies with unilateral expression, bilateral expression, and no expression (data not shown).
mapping_basis: The paper's name DNa02 is the MANC type name in type_list.csv; Methods name SS00730 (DNa02 in driver_lines.csv).
stimulation: 617 nm light from above the head, symmetric, 68 uW/mm2, 0.5 s every 11 s, 150 trials
type_coverage: bilateral expression (both DNa02), scored post hoc by dissection
sensory_condition: walking on spherical treadmill; head cuticle intact, no dissection before behaviour
n_flies_note: Fig. 8B legend: 17 bilateral flies; Methods: 47 brains with bilateral expression
notes: Bilaterally expressing siblings were stimulated in the same way and used as the null. Their light-evoked forward-velocity changes matched those of no-expression flies (data not shown; attributed to visual startle), and by construction they showed no directional bias. The outcome differs from the unilateral group, so it is a separate record. Flies were already walking and legs were not tracked, so leg fields are not_assessed. Confidence is low because the data are not shown.
